notes: Mark FC when multiple pops occur close together; hold settings. Don't increase heat to chase a brief FC dip. Decaf: FC comes early (EA decafs cracked at 178-183) and quieter than regular beans.

history.change: Initial procedure, copied from Honduran MWP Decaf (current version): charge burner 45 / SV 230; burner 40 at 150, 35 + air 40 at 175, 30 at 189, 25 at 196; drop at 202.8. The reference is #29 (Honduran MWP, the same steps); there is no roast of this bean yet.
history.why: Untried bean, so this starts from the most similar one with history. Burman's Decaffeinated Mexican Esmeralda EA Natural (part of the 3 lb decaf bundle; Burman Coffee order #335002 (2026-10-14), 1 lb, 3 batches): Mexican beans, decaffeinated with ethyl acetate (the 'natural' sugarcane EA process, about 97% of the caffeine removed). Crisp citrus when blonde; smooth and rich with chocolate and floral aromatics at medium; strong, slightly sweet, rich chocolate when dark. Burman says it roasts easily from light to dark: stop before second crack for a sweeter cup, go into it for a heavier, baker's chocolate cup. The listing gives no region, variety, altitude or screen size. The only EA decaf with history is Colombia Huila EA Decaf (#3, #6, #9, #14, #26, #35, no procedure): run with older Artisan settings, its later roasts cracked at 178-183 around 6:45 and dropped at 202.0-202.4 around 9:24-10:02, nearly the Honduran MWP's timing. So this uses the Honduran MWP Decaf procedure, our only decaf procedure, whose 202.8 drop made an excellent latte (#29) and a REALLY GOOD half-caf latte (#34), and keeps the drop before second crack for the sweeter cup Burman describes. #29 is the reference because it ran these steps. First guess; adjust after tasting.
